summary:
What if children could experience the challenges of space exploration instead of simply reading about them?

MOONSHIFT: Beyond Earth is a story-driven, interactive 2D space adventure created by "The Side Quest Squad" for young explorers aged 7–12.

Across three interconnected environments—the Moon, an orbital space station, and Mars—players become junior astronauts responsible for solving realistic, NASA-inspired engineering challenges.

Through interactive missions, players investigate life-support failures, recycle water, distribute electricity, grow food, navigate rovers, restore communications, and respond to environmental hazards.

Our five main characters represent actual members of our team—Fatema, Eyad, Abdelrahman, Rawan, and Rewaa—and feature our own recorded voices, making the experience personal and original.

By combining exploration, engaging gameplay, scientific problem-solving, and NASA research, MOONSHIFT transforms complex concepts into accessible learning experiences.

Our goal is to inspire the next generation of explorers by allowing children to think, experiment, and learn like astronauts.
details:
When we started working on MOONSHIFT, we had one question in mind: What if kids could experience what it's like to be an astronaut instead of just learning about space from books and videos?

That's how MOONSHIFT: Beyond Earth came to life. We wanted to make space science exciting, interactive, and easy to understand for children aged 7–12. So, we created a story-driven 2D adventure where players become junior astronauts, explore different environments, and solve the kinds of challenges astronauts and engineers face in space.

The journey takes players through three worlds: the Moon, an orbital space station, and Mars. Each has its own challenges, from managing electricity and recycling water to growing plants, navigating rovers, restoring communications, and protecting the crew from environmental hazards.

We didn't want the game to feel like a science quiz with a space background. We wanted players to actually do things: repair systems, operate equipment, make decisions, and see what happens when something goes wrong. The idea is that every mission teaches something useful while still being fun to play.

One of our favorite parts of the project is that the five main characters are actually us: Fatema, Eyad, Abdelrahman, Rawan, and Rewaa. We brought ourselves into the story and recorded our own voices for the characters. It made the whole experience feel much more personal, like we're going on this adventure together with the player.

We also wanted the science to be meaningful. We used NASA research on life-support systems, water recovery, space agriculture, astronaut health, planetary exploration, and communications to shape the challenges. For example, NASA's work on recycling water aboard the International Space Station inspired one of our missions, where players investigate and restore a simulated water-processing system. We simplified some mechanics to make them accessible to younger players while keeping the underlying scientific ideas accurate.

To build the game, we used HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and HTML5 Canvas, with GitHub for managing our code and Vercel for deployment. We also used AI tools to help with development, debugging, and design, while directing the concept, story, characters, and gameplay ourselves.

Beyond the main adventure, we've worked on features like science questions after missions, Credits, achievements, character customization, and optional emergency scenarios to make learning more rewarding and encourage players to keep exploring.

What makes MOONSHIFT special to us isn't just the technology or the visuals. It's the idea that a child could finish a mission feeling excited because they figured something out themselves.

We hope MOONSHIFT encourages more kids to become curious about space, ask questions, experiment, and maybe even imagine themselves becoming the scientists, engineers, and astronauts of the future.

Because sometimes, the best way to learn about space is to feel like you're actually there.
